nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, the statement that for every colouring of the natural numbers with two colours there is a monochromatic $k$-term descending wave all of whose terms lie in $\{1, \dots, n\}$. Equivalently, every colouring of $\{1, \dots, n\}$ with two colours has a monochromatic $k$-term descending wave, so the statement says $f(k) \le n$, where $f(k)$ is the least $n$ with this property.
nodes.title: Forcing a monochromatic descending wave

nodes.summary: A $k$-term descending wave is a sequence $x_0, x_1, \dots, x_{k-1}$ of natural numbers with $x_0 < x_1 < \dots < x_{k-1}$ and $x_{j-1} + x_{j+1} \le 2 x_j$ for every $j$ with $0 < j < k - 1$.

nodes.title: Erdős Problem 781 is false

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, say that $n$ forces a $k$-term wave if every colouring of $\{1, \dots, n\}$ with two colours has a monochromatic $k$-term descending wave. The statement that for every natural number $k \ge 1$ the number $k^2 - k + 1$ forces a $k$-term wave and the number $k^2 - k$ does not; that is, $f(k) = k^2 - k + 1$ for every $k \ge 1$, where $f(k)$ is the least $n$ that forces a $k$-term wave.
